A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same online inverse linear optimization work. Their complete text, equations, algorithms, figures and appendices support comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 contains theoretical algorithms, regret bounds, proofs and geometric illustrations, but no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: V6 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. Its new Table 1 compares asymptotic guarantees and computational complexity, not empirical measurements.

M1.justification: The ONS and MetaGrad designs are retained, but Appendix B.3 changes MetaGrad's dyadic learning-rate grid endpoint from ceil((ln T)/2) to ceil((log_2 T)/2). This changes the number and range of experts and is a limited algorithmic correction. The two-dimensional algorithm is retained in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Neither version trains on or evaluates datasets. The inverse optimization settings and constructed instances are studied theoretically.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. The newly included Gollapudi comparison in Table 1 and Appendix A concerns theoretical guarantees and complexity.

E3.justification: Neither version reports empirical evaluation protocols, training budgets or testing procedures. The revised feasible-set normalization in Appendix C is a theorem assumption, not an experimental setting.

E4.justification: Robustness to suboptimal feedback remains a theoretical guarantee in Section 4. Neither version contains ablations, empirical robustness tests or experimental case studies; the geometric discussion is retained in Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run statistics, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. Expectations in the regret bounds concern theoretical randomness.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical performance values, measured runtimes or experimental findings. The new Table 1 summarizes theoretical bounds rather than experimental results.

T1.justification: The principal regret bounds are retained. However, v6 tightens the two-dimensional result's feasible-set radius from 1 to 1/2, supporting the proof's unit-diameter bound; Theorem 6.2 becomes Theorem C.2. It also corrects the lower-bound proof's quantifier order and strengthens the MetaGrad grid argument. Appendix A adds a computational-cost derivation for the prior centroid method. These are local corrections and extensions rather than new main theorems.

C1.justification: V1 presents O(n ln T) as improving the best-known O(n^4 ln T) bound by n^3. V6 acknowledges Gollapudi et al.'s existing O(n ln T) bound and instead claims the first logarithmic-regret method with T-independent per-round complexity. The two-dimensional finite-regret result also ceases to be a headline contribution.

C2.justification: V6 explains that previously known finite regret with exponential dimension dependence makes its two-dimensional result an illustrative analysis. The new conclusion discusses possible gradient-norm tradeoffs and finite polynomial regret when line-segment feasible sets are revealed before prediction. Existing explanations of suboptimal feedback and higher-dimensional geometric obstacles remain.

D1.justification: V6's MetaGrad pseudocode explicitly sends both the aggregate prediction w_t and gradient g_t to each expert, whereas v1 sends only g_t. This clarifies implementation of the surrogate loss, which already depended on both quantities in v1.

R1.justification: Adding Gollapudi et al. (2021) substantially changes the nearest-prior-work account and novelty positioning. V6 also expands contextual-search, corruption-robustness and online-portfolio literature, and Appendix A develops a detailed comparison of centroid-based computation. These changes go substantially beyond citation or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around computational efficiency. Related work expands, a conclusion is added, and the former Section 6 becomes Appendix C. Together these changes substantially reorganize the paper's narrative.

P2.justification: V6 adds Table 1 comparing theoretical regret and computational complexity. Figures 1–2 and the two-dimensional pseudocode move to Appendix C, preserving the diagrams. Typography, captions and algorithm numbering are also revised.

improvement.justification: V6 resolves a central novelty overstatement by acknowledging Gollapudi et al.'s existing O(n ln T) bound and identifying computational efficiency as its contribution, supported by Table 1 and Appendix A. The corrected MetaGrad grid and feasible-set assumption also strengthen mathematical reliability. These changes substantially improve the paper's accuracy and positioning while retaining its principal guarantees.
